chalisa.do1: Salutations, salutations to you, Vindhyeśvarī; salutations, salutations to you, Mother of the world.
In the work of the saints you make no delay.
chalisa.cau1: Victory, victory, victory to you, queen of the Vindhya mountains, primal Śakti, Bhavānī known to all the world.
chalisa.cau2: Victory to you, Mother of the world, who ride the lion; victory, victory, victory to you, who give joy to the three worlds.
chalisa.cau3: Victory to you, goddess of the world, who remove distress; victory, victory to you, whom saints, demons and gods serve.
chalisa.cau4: Your glory is boundless, without end; Śeṣa with his thousand mouths gave up describing it.
chalisa.cau5: Bhavānī, you take away the sorrows of the humble; no giver like you has been seen.
chalisa.cau6: Mother, you fulfil the wishes of all; your boundless glory is famed throughout the world.
chalisa.cau7: Whoever fixes his meditation on you at once gains the fruit he desires.
chalisa.cau8: You are Vaiṣṇavī, you are Rudrāṇī; you are Śāradā and Brahmāṇī.
chalisa.cau9: You are Ramā, Rādhikā, Śyāmā and Kālī; you, Mother, are the protector of the saints.
chalisa.cau10: Umā, Mādhavī, Caṇḍī, Jvālā, be merciful to me soon.
chalisa.cau11: You are the great queen of Hiṅgalāja; you are Śītalā, and the knower of truth.
chalisa.cau12: You are Mother Durgā, destroyer of hardship; you are Lakṣmī, who gives joy to the world.
chalisa.cau13: You are Jāhnavī and Utrāṇī; you are Haimavatī, the Mother who grants liberation.
chalisa.cau14: You are the eight-armed goddess Vārāhī, whom Viṣṇu and Śiva serve.
chalisa.cau15: You are the sixty-four goddesses, Kalyāṇī, Gaurī and Maṅgalā, a mine of every virtue.
chalisa.cau16: Pāṭan, Mumbā, Danta Kumārī and Bhadrakālī, hear our prayer.
chalisa.cau17: You are the bearer of the thunderbolt, the destroyer of grief, the guardian of life, Vindhyavāsinī.
chalisa.cau18: You are Jayā and Vijayā, Vaitālī, Mother Saṅkaṭā and Vikarālī, the fearsome one.
chalisa.cau19: Bhavānī, your names are endless; how can an ignorant man describe them?
chalisa.cau20: Mother, the one on whom your grace falls does whatever his heart desires.
chalisa.cau21: Be gracious to me, great queen; now make these words of mine come true.
chalisa.cau22: The man who meditates on the Mother always fares well.
chalisa.cau23: Calamity does not come, even in a dream, to one who has the Goddess's japa performed.
chalisa.cau24: A man who has boundless debts should recite this a hundred times.
chalisa.cau25: Release from debt surely comes to the man who recites it with his mind intent.
chalisa.cau26: The man who reads this hymn of praise and has others read it finds great happiness in this world.
chalisa.cau27: Brother, if illness torments someone, all of it flees as he recites the japa.
chalisa.cau28: The man who lies in harsh captivity should recite it a thousand times.
chalisa.cau29: He is surely freed from captivity; brother, believe my words, which are true.
chalisa.cau30: Whoever is in any trouble should remember the Goddess, without fail.
chalisa.cau31: Brother, a man who has no son should take this remedy, in this way.
chalisa.cau32: For five years he should have the recitation done, and in the Navarātras feed Brahmins.
chalisa.cau33: Bhavānī will surely be pleased, and give him a son who is a mine of virtues.
chalisa.cau34: He should come and offer a banner and a coconut, and have worship done with the proper rites.
chalisa.cau35: Let him recite it every day with his mind intent and with love; there is no other means.
chalisa.cau36: This is the Śrī Vindhyācala Chālīsā; a pauper who reads it becomes a king.
chalisa.cau37: Brother, do not count this a wonder when her gracious glance has fallen on someone.
chalisa.cau38: Victory, victory, victory to you, Bhavānī, Mother of the world; knowing me as your servant, be gracious to me.
